messages:
maya: FYI pushed a small change to the continuous-batcher admission logic that ties token_budget_target to decode_rate_bucket instead of raw prompt_len
toni: Nice — short summary of why?
maya: We were seeing KV thrash when short prompts joined long ones; long prompts would dominate the KV warmup and flip kernels mid-batch causing tail latency spikes
samir: Can you show the old vs new heuristic?
maya: Old: prefer fill-to-N-tokens, no decode-rate awareness. New: compute target_tokens = clamp(bucket_target[decode_rate_bucket], min_tokens, max_tokens) and admit up to target but prefer homogenous decode-rate cohorts
maya: ```json
{"bucket_target": {"slow": 256, "medium": 128, "fast": 64}, "min_tokens": 8, "max_tokens": 512}
```
toni: Ran a quick canary on the ft-qa workload. p95 latency dropped 12% for medium bucket, p99 unchanged. Throughput +3% overall.
bec: Any regressions observed?
maya: On a mixed streaming workload we saw a 1.8% drop in token/s; digging in traces shows extra microbatches created when an admitted short prompt hit an ongoing long prompt kernel path
samir: So admission defers mixing that case?
maya: Exactly — cohorting by decode_rate reduces kernel flips. Also adjusted KV prefetch window to avoid evicting >1 top-level KV segment during warmup
maya: kv-prefetch change: reduce aggressive_prefetch_cutoff from 0.75 -> 0.5 for long sequences, this keeps older segments resident longer
toni: Can you paste the trace snippet where kernel flip shows up?
maya: ```
[trace] batch_id=0x7a3f decode_kernel=fast -> switched to matmul-tiling after kv-warmup, tail_latency=210ms
[trace] batch_id=0x7a4c homogeneous batch (medium) kernel=matmul-streaming tail_latency=88ms
```
bec: Good to have concrete numbers. What's the plan for kernel selection mapping?
maya: We introduced a lightweight hybrid selector: if cohort_entropy < 0.2 and avg_decode_rate > threshold -> prefer fast-kernel; else prefer stable-kernel which tolerates long KV warmups. Selector config lives in runtime/selector/v2.yaml (I'll open PR)
samir: Any perf regression test failures? CI flagged a 2% p50 regression on small-embed bench when selector toggles; might be noise but worth a targeted run
toni: Re-ran targeted bench with seed and same infra, regression disappears. suspecting noisier host scheduling on first run
maya: Action items: 1) roll selector config to canary with traffic-split 5% for next 48h, 2) add a KV warmup metric to console (kv_warmup_evictions count), 3) add a small-workload A/B to make sure small embedded requests don't regress
bec: I'll own the dashboard metric. samir can you do the canary rollout?
samir: Yep — scheduling the split now. infra-bot: Deployment canary scheduled: canary_id=cb-335987, split=5%, start=2026-03-18T15:12:00Z
maya: Thanks — will monitor p50/p95 and kv_warmup_evictions. If p99 or kv_evictions spike, auto-rollback enabled. :thumbsup:
toni: TL;DR: cohort by decode_rate + conservative kv-prefetch reduces kernel flips and lowers tail for medium workloads with small perf/noise risk on tiny embed cases
bec: ack, will add alerts for kv_evictions > 10/min
maya: closing loop — I'll post PR link when ready and attach baseline/patch traces
